messages.subject: adding objects to stack
parts:
Hello everyone, 
I would like to create a model with a random walk effect of depth (depth = depth1) onto two different length classes ("small", "large"), which I created as following:
subset_fData$small <- as.numeric(subset_fData$size == 1) 
subset_fData$large <- as.numeric(subset_fData$size == 2)

This is how I defined the model: 
f2 <- parse(text=c("y ~ -1 + Intercept +",paste(c(names(X2)[!names(X2)=="lsurface"],"offset(lsurface)",
   ' f(depth, large, model="rw1", hyper=list(prec=list(initial=4.66)))',' f(depth1, small, model="rw1", hyper=list(prec=list(initial=4.66)))',
    " f(w, model = spde)"   ),collapse =" + ")))

stack definition: 
Stk2 <- inla.stack(tag = "Fit",
                 data = list(y = subset_fData$NoAtLength),
                 A = list(1,1,1,1,A2),
                 effects = list(
                   Intercept=rep(1,N), 
                   X2 = X2,
                   depth = subset_fData$bot_vs,
                   depth1 = subset_fData$bot_vs1,
                   w = w2.index))


However, "large" and "small" can not be found (obviously because I didn't define them in the stack), when I run the model (data = inla.stack.data(Stk2)). I tried to add them into the data part. But this didn't solve my problem. 
Stk2 <- inla.stack(tag = "Fit",
                 data = list(y = subset_fData$NoAtLength, small = subset_fData$small, large = subset_fData$large),
                 A = list(1,1,1,1,A2),
                 effects = list(
                   Intercept=rep(1,N), 
                   X2 = X2,
                   depth = subset_fData$bot_vs,
                   depth1 = subset_fData$bot_vs1,
                   w = w2.index))

So my question is how do I add those objects into the stack?

Thanks in advance, 
Bram

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] adding objects to stack
parts:
Hi,
Since you’re just using large and small as multiplicative weights, you can
Instead apply them as Diagonal A-matrices in the stack construction, which has the same effect.
So instead of specifying 1 as A matrix for depth1, use Diagonal(length(small), small)), etc.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] adding objects to stack
parts:
Hi, by incorporating the weights into the A matrices, you should no longer specify any weights in the f() specifications.

Finn
